note: All events of type 'earthquake' with preferred magnitude >= 6.0 in ComCat, 1900-2025 (14356 events). Magnitude is the catalogue's preferred magnitude (about 90% moment magnitude Mw; most pre-1973 events come from the ISC-GEM catalogue, the rest mostly from the USGS NEIC), rounded to 1 decimal; positions rounded to 0.01 deg. The early decades are less complete: fewer seismographs recorded fewer moderate (M6) events, so rising counts before about 1960 reflect better detection, not more earthquakes. 6857 events (47%, nearly all before 1973) are contributed to ComCat by the ISC-GEM Global Instrumental Earthquake Catalogue (International Seismological Centre and GEM Foundation, CC BY-SA 3.0); the rest are USGS or US regional network solutions (US public domain). Ten largest: 1960-05-22 1960 Great Chilean Earthquake (Valdivia Earthquake) M9.5; 1964-03-28 The 1964 Prince William Sound, Alaska Earthquake M9.2; 2004-12-26 2004 Sumatra - Andaman Islands Earthquake M9.1; 2011-03-11 2011 Great Tohoku Earthquake, Japan M9.1; 1952-11-04 89 km ESE of Petropavlovsk-Kamchatsky, Russia M9.0; 1906-01-31 1906 Ecuador-Colombia Earthquake M8.8; 2010-02-27 2010 Maule, Chile Earthquake M8.8; 2025-07-29 2025 Kamchatka Peninsula, Russia Earthquake M8.8; 1965-02-04 1965 Western Aleutian Islands (Hawadax/Rat Islands) Earthquake M8.7; 1946-04-01 The 1946 Unimak Island, Alaska Earthquake M8.6. Events per decade: 1900s 350, 1910s 684, 1920s 966, 1930s 1073, 1940s 964, 1950s 1298, 1960s 1267, 1970s 1093, 1980s 1257, 1990s 1530, 2000s 1585, 2010s 1493, 2020s (to 2025) 796.
